thread:
Jamie (Customer): Hey team — high-priority customer on Dedicated reporting streaming hangs in their Next.js edge deployment. Behavior: client starts ReadableStream from ts-sdk, receives a few chunks, then stream "closed" early and no more data. Happens consistently ~90s after connection for some flows. Request id: r-abc123. Node 18, Next edge, ts-sdk@0.7.0. Auth uses short-lived token with rotation via middleware. Can escalate please?

Alex (Support): Thanks Jamie — can you paste minimal repro and the exact SDK version from package-lock/yarn.lock? Is this hosted or dedicated/private? Any billing/duplicate charge issues when retries happen?

Jamie (Customer): It's Dedicated VPC. package.json: "@redwood/inference": "0.7.0" (ts-sdk alias). Code: ```js
// server/edge/api/stream.js
const res = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', messages });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  processChunk(value);
}
```
Token rotation handled by middleware that swaps the header on each fetch.

Alex (Support): ok, adding eng runtime: Maria (Eng Runtime) — can you take a look?

Maria (Eng Runtime): looking. Quick question: does the token get swapped mid-stream (i.e., the same connection sees a new Authorization header)? Also any gateway/proxy (Vercel/Cloudflare) in front?

Jamie (Customer): Yes token rotates via internal hook at ~60s. They deploy on Vercel edge (Next edge runtime) in front of our Dedicated gateway. We see 503 from gateway in logs right before client sees closed stream.

Maria (Eng Runtime): hmm. Repro idea: if the SDK mutates the Authorization header for in-flight SSE/ReadableStream requests, some proxies will sever the connection (401/503 path). Can you paste the gateway logs around r-abc123?

Jamie (Customer): Gateway excerpt: ```
[2026-02-19T12:04:21Z] r-abc123 incoming conn established
[2026-02-19T12:05:53Z] r-abc123 backend returned 503, reason="upstream-auth-failed"
[2026-02-19T12:05:53Z] r-abc123 connection closed to client
```

Alex (Support): that matches client symptom. Kevin (Oncall) joining to check runtime traces.

Kevin (Oncall): I ran local repro against edge-like env with ts-sdk@0.7.0 and see same early close when we trigger token refresh midway. Root cause looks like a regression in how the Node/edge adapter re-injects headers for streaming sockets — some code path swaps headers and triggers backend to reject connection. I can reproduce in ~30s with a simple rotation script.

Kevin (Oncall): Quick workaround: pin to ts-sdk@0.6.2 or ensure token TTL > streaming duration to avoid mid-stream rotation. We'll patch the adapter.

Alex (Support): Can you share a small repro script we can run internally? Jamie — would prefer a tiny script we can run without your full app.

Jamie (Customer): created minimal repro gist: https://internal.gists/stream-rotation-repro (contains edge-like fetch + token swap timer).

Maria (Eng Runtime): thanks — I pulled the gist. For immediate mitigation: if you can't extend tokens, try client-side: catch stream close with code to re-open and seek using server-side resume tokens (conversation state). Not ideal but buys time.

Alex (Support): Jamie — we also saw customer report duplicate billing on retried streams where the SDK retried on 502/503 and the app also retried. Priya (Billing) — can you watch for duplicate charge flags for r-abc123?

Priya (Billing): noted, I'll correlate charges for customer's account and flag any duplicates. Please pass any request IDs.

Kevin (Oncall): Engineering plan: 1) Patch header mutation in adapter (will prevent mid-stream header swap) 2) Add a defensive retry only on idempotent failures for streaming and avoid double-count in SDK retry logic 3) Add telemetry event `stream_premature_close` with reason. Will push a canary fix to hosted and a patch release 0.7.1 within 3 hours.

Maria (Eng Runtime): quick patch (internal) to stop header rebind is ready — canary deploy in ~10m to hosted. For Dedicated customers, we have a config patch we'll stage to the gateway to accept existing connections during token refresh window.

Alex (Support): Jamie, once canary is out, can you try hitting the hosted test endpoint or we can provide a canary build of ts-sdk (0.7.1-canary.1) to validate in your Dedicated environment?

Jamie (Customer): can try canary SDK. Would prefer not to change infra. If you can provide a canary package we can test today that'd be great.

Kevin (Oncall): publishing 0.7.1-canary.1 to our internal npm registry now — it includes header-freeze fix for streaming. I'll DM access. Expect to see improvement; we'll also add a temporary edge-level rule to avoid 503 on midstream auth swap.

SRE Bot: Created trace id trace-2523450007-1 and started capture for r-abc123.

Maria (Eng Runtime): follow-ups: 1) we want logs from customer's SDK showing response headers and any 401/503 for the exact request id 2) we need to confirm client runtime (edge vs serverless) so we can reproduce with correct fetch polyfills.

Jamie (Customer): grabbing SDK logs and will upload. Thanks for quick triage.

Alex (Support): looping back on billing — Priya will escalate if duplicates found. For now will mark this P1 support escalation and track internally.

Priya (Billing): got the ids. If duplicates exist we'll credit and follow up.

Jamie (Customer): installed canary, ran 10 tests — streams now stay open for >5m, no 503s so far. Will run load tests and confirm tomorrow. Thanks folks! :tada:

Alex (Support): great news — leaving open until Jamie confirms load test. Will convert to bug report and post-mortem if confirmed.

Kevin (Oncall): created internal bug ID BUG-4301. Patch will be included in next stable (0.7.1). Will add postmortem if billing duplicates are confirmed.

Jamie (Customer): thanks everyone — I'll update once load tests complete.
